dedupe_keys.name: dense air temperature measurement campaigns in two leipzig parks during the 2018 and 2019 heat and drought summers ufz

description: These campaigns measured air temperature at many points inside and around two inner-city parks in Leipzig, Germany, Friedenspark (17.5 ha) and Lene-Voigt-Park (5.8 ha), during the heat and drought summers of 2018 and 2019, to quantify how green spaces cool their surroundings. Roland Kraemer, Paul Remmler, Jan Bumberger and Nadja Kabisch of the Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research and Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin describe the design, sensors, logistics, calibration and data management in a MethodsX protocol article published in May 2022. Coverage is the two parks and their vicinity. Format and access: calibrated Level-1 logger data from Onset HOBO U23-002 sensors, which the article says were deposited in a public repository, plus a dashboard for long-term stations. Licence: the article is CC-BY-4.0; the data licence was not read; free. Caveats: two summers at two parks, and the data deposit was not opened in this session. It supports climate adaptation studies by providing observations to calibrate and validate park cooling in urban climate models. Related catalogue records are the Blue Green Wave green roof data and the NGIF sensor data.
